correctness.rationale: The exact-domain claim is reconstructed for all integers d>=1, q>=2. The local-ball coordinate-group lemma controls all four-point supports and classifies every candidate triple into three mutually disjoint coordinate types. Explicit centers realize each required trace whenever stated; for d=2 the missing empty trace is proved impossible at q=3 and available at q>=4. Counts have unique centers and collapse by Pascal identity to q^d(q-1)^3 binom(d+1,3). Singleton/pair exceptions are proved. A standard-library checker independently enumerates traces for sixteen small cases and reproduces the polynomial, including four-point non-shattering. Computation is not used to claim an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The class of radius-one q-ary Hamming balls is central in coding and graph neighborhood VC analysis. Knowing only VC dimension three cannot recover the all-size shattering profile or counts. The theorem gives an exact natural invariant over every alphabet size and dimension and an explicit coordinate-geometry decomposition; it also pinpoints the nontrivial two-coordinate exceptional progression q=2,3,4. It is a complete classification, not a tiny numerical increment or arbitrary subcase.
